dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "DLR-104/DLR-219 annual renewals (Mar–Jun only) post on month-end dates while effective_event_date spreads across the month (32/50 and 22/40 rows mismatched) | recharges.csv"
"May annual volume (8 & 9) sits inside the normal 4–12/dealer/month range seen Jan–Jun | recharges.csv"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31 May cluster is a legitimate, contract-permitted batch-posting artifact from two West dealers (DLR-104, DLR-219) who submit annual-plan renewal files monthly rather than daily."
"the posted/effective mismatch is isolated to annual-plan rows for exactly the two dealers named in the email"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "No dealer_id→name mapping file to formally confirm DLR-104/219 = Silver Dish Services/Metro Signal Point"
"Cause of the Jan/Feb→March shift from daily to monthly submission is unstated."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Pull the dealer-contract amendment confirming DLR-104/DLR-219's monthly annual-file cadence and verify the dealer-ID-to-name mapping"
"no reversal of postings needed, since every month reconciles to $0 variance."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Duplicate revenue — rejected: 0 duplicate_source_event_ids logged; all 17 May source_event_ids unique; no repeat subscribers in the batch."
"Pipeline defect — rejected: the posted/effective mismatch is isolated to annual-plan rows for exactly the two dealers named in the email"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "It is not duplicate revenue, not manipulated reporting, and not a system pipeline defect." The reconciliation and uniqueness checks strongly reduce duplicate-revenue risk, but do not conclusively exclude manipulation or a dealer-specific ingestion/configuration defect.
"rules out a system-wide bug" supports exclusion of a broad system-wide defect, not the stronger conclusion that there is no pipeline defect of any kind.
"contractually submit annual-plan files monthly" is attributed to the dealer email, while the submission itself acknowledges that the contract amendment has not been verified.
"No reversal of postings needed" is reasonable for financial reconciliation, but the submission does not address whether downstream event-time analytics require correction or a field change.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A dealer-specific pipeline or configuration defect, or an unauthorized change in submission cadence, could produce the same localized annual-plan pattern even if cash reconciles. The submission partly handles the latter through its proposed contract-amendment check, but does not explicitly test the former. It also misses the important alternative that the postings are financially benign while still distorting month-based retention or renewal analytics.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add an explicit downstream-analytics safeguard: use effective_event_date for event-time reporting and test dealer-specific ingestion/configuration and contract-change history before treating the posting pattern as fully explained.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South weekly tickets fall from ~40–58/wk (pre-May) to ~14–28/wk (post-May 10), while N/W/E regions stay flat or rise over the same window — a real, region-specific drop, not a company-wide trend" (tickets.csv)
"Under NOVA-S1 (South), 24.0% of IVR sessions terminate at the authenticate stage (650/2,709), vs 7.9% under LEGACY (35/442)" (ivr_interactions.jsonl)

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The South complaint-case drop is not reliable evidence of improved customer experience — it is largely a reporting artifact of (a) a policy that excludes pre-authentication sessions from CareDesk case counts, and (b) a sharp rise in authentication failures/abandonment under NovaIVR that hides real unresolved contacts from the ticket data."
"South AGENT_DIRECT-origin tickets collapse post-pilot ... while IVR-origin tickets stay flat ... — consistent with calls being rerouted into NovaIVR and lost there, not resolved"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Unknown: whether auth-stage ERROR/ABANDONED sessions represent genuine unresolved complaints or low-stakes queries the customer didn't retry — no repeat-contact linkage available in current files."
"Genuine self-service success (as sole explanation) — rejected ..."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."

"Pull the technical pilot report Farah's email references and match its session IDs against tickets.csv/repeat-contact records before any expansion decision; do not change routing or dashboard definitions in the meantime."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What does the technical pilot report show for the 650 South sessions that ended at the authenticate stage — are any of those later linked to a case or repeat contact?"
"Can you provide sampled call recordings or logs for 10–15 South sessions that ended in ABANDONED or ERROR at authentication"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "It is largely a reporting artifact" is stronger than the available evidence because the submission does not yet link failed sessions to unresolved outcomes or establish how many would otherwise have become complaints.

"hides real unresolved contacts" and "lost there, not resolved" infer unresolved customer outcomes from authentication errors and abandonment; the submission appropriately acknowledges that this remains unknown.
"rules out a network-outage confound" is too absolute: stable service-event volume weakens that explanation but does not rule out every other service or demand confound.

The assertion that balance_check/pack_info traffic is "routine self-service" and not "case-worthy" is plausible from the stage labels but is not directly validated with journey outcomes or sampled calls.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative: the pilot may have produced genuine self-service success, particularly because case_create share fell while balance_check/pack_info volume rose. It also preserved the possibility that authentication abandonment involved low-stakes queries that customers did not retry, rather than complaints. The remaining gap is direct validation of successful journey completion and customer impact for those sessions.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add an explicit end-to-end denominator and linkage analysis: for each South IVR cohort and outcome, match session IDs to later cases, repeat contacts, dealer visits, or other resolution records, supplemented by sampled call review. This would quantify unresolved friction rather than relying on abandonment as a proxy.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission explicitly cites inverter_events.csv for the claims that all four events are cleared, have impact_mw=0, and last no more than seven minutes.
It cites the same file for the warning/info severity breakdown and the absence of repeated inverters.
The quoted claim “COMM_LINK_WARN on INV-17 (27 May, 7 min, cleared, 0 MW impact)” is specific and distinguishes the observed event attributes from the recommendation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission uses several relevant fields together—repeat inverter identity, clearance status, duration, MW impact, and severity—to assess the equipment-fault-cluster hypothesis.
It appropriately states that “event-type wording like FAN_SPEED_HIGH isn't itself evidence of failure,” avoiding an anomaly-to-cause leap.
Reasoning is primarily based on one CSV channel and does not independently corroborate communications health or plant output beyond the file's impact_mw field.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission is appropriately restrained in saying the event is “worth a quick recurrence check, not escalation” and identifies the small four-row sample as a limitation.
It explicitly asks whether the export is full and unfiltered, which is a material uncertainty.

The phrase “This is a developing equipment-fault cluster is rejected” is somewhat too categorical for only four events over approximately one week; the evidence more precisely shows that the visible file does not support that hypothesis.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “confirm the export filter behind inverter_events.csv” is low-cost, operationally proportionate, and directly addresses the main uncertainty.
The proposed check is discriminating: it can determine whether the low event volume reflects a narrowed export rather than actual low volume.
The submission correctly avoids escalation despite the seven-minute communications warning because the event cleared with zero MW impact.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion “Nothing here warrants escalation” fits the observed zero-MW impact, cleared status, short duration, and lack of repeated inverters.
The conclusion remains scoped to the visible file and pairs non-escalation with a sensible completeness check rather than treating the small sample as definitive reassurance.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “This is a developing equipment-fault cluster is rejected” overstates what can be concluded from only four rows; the file does not support the hypothesis, but cannot strongly rule out future development.
“No inverter repeats across the file” is valid only for the supplied export and should not be generalized beyond its date, filter, and scope.
The analysis does not independently verify plant output or communications performance outside the CSV's recorded impact_mw and cleared fields.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent quiet period may be an artifact of a narrowed, filtered, or incomplete export rather than genuinely low event volume; if the export is complete, the visible evidence is more consistent with isolated transient events than a developing equipment fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the cluster conclusion explicitly conditional on export completeness and phrase it as “not supported by the visible sample” rather than “rejected”; then perform the proposed filter/date/inverter/severity-scope check.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv for recomputed 28/29 May sums, the 12/96 pilot_revision blocks, stow counts, wind, generation, and schedule totals.
It cites DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for the claim that intraday revision is a standard commercial option.

The submission does not calculate the required same-day 29 May counterfactual penalty using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw; it reports only aggregate base and submitted schedule totals.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It triangulates whole-day results, block-level schedule-source mix, stow counts, weather, generation, a 4 June conventional comparison, and the DSM rules extract.
It tests an innocent operational explanation by arguing that the schedule revision was available to conventional workflows.

The statement that “physical stow actions were identical” is stronger than the cited evidence of identical stow block counts; similar counts do not establish identical timing, magnitude, or operational effect.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly distinguishes “the number itself is real” from causal attribution and calls the 31.6% result an N=1 day-pair comparison.
It identifies unresolved questions about the 12 pilot-revision blocks and firmware differences, and recommends not treating 31.6% as a validated causal KPI.
It preserves the possibility that the pilot has value rather than concluding that the pilot is ineffective.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to continue collecting paired observations while withholding external causal claims follows from the limited evidence.
The proposed next measurement—comparing the 12 pilot-revision blocks with same-clock-time blocks on 28 May, 3 June, and 4 June—is discriminating and directly addresses schedule-source attribution.
The recommendation preserves the operational pilot rather than imposing an unsupported stop.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly states that the 31.6% reduction is arithmetically reproducible but not causally established.
It notices that the comparison uses different days and identifies the smaller, defensible claim that the AI-assisted day performed better on the observed day-pair.
It appropriately attributes much of the observed difference provisionally to scheduling changes while retaining uncertainty about whether the pilot contributed.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Physical stow actions were identical between the two days” is not fully supported by identical stow block counts alone; the cited evidence does not establish identical stow timing, magnitude, or operational consequences.

“Most of the gap shrinkage traces to an intraday schedule revision” is plausible from the aggregate schedule totals, but it is not demonstrated without calculating the 29 May base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw penalty counterfactual.
The claim that the 4 June day had “similar wind” should be tied to explicit wind statistics and matched conditions rather than treated as dispositive evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have contributed indirectly by enabling or improving the 29 May intraday schedule revision, even if the revision was technically available to conventional workflows. The 4 June comparison and identical stow counts weaken a direct wind-stow mechanism, but they do not rule out a scheduling or decision-support effect from the pilot's 12 blocks.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compute the same-day 29 May counterfactual by applying the DSM penalty calculation to base_schedule_mw instead of submitted_schedule_mw, preferably block by block, then compare that result with the submitted-schedule outcome and matched clock-time blocks on the other high-wind days.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Swiss Matrix's current approved code for P1001 is 90211000, effective 2025-01-01, no end date — an exact match to the declaration"
"Helios Commodity Code (90211090) is explicitly documented as a migration-mapped default used \"where a local approved code was not supplied,\" not a Swiss-specific value"
"No Swiss duty-rate table by code exists in these files"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "The mismatch only appears against an EU-oriented master code that the data owner itself says isn't expected to match Swiss entries."
"A ruling mandating 90211090 instead would reverse this judgment."
"EU countries' approved CN8 for P1001 is 90211090 (matching Helios), confirming 90211090 is the EU-side code, not the Swiss one"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "No Swiss duty-rate table by code exists in these files, so we can't independently confirm 90211000 and 90211090 carry the same duty treatment"
"Also unconfirmed: whether Switzerland's 90211000 row reflects a formal Tares ruling or only an internal working classification"
"A ruling mandating 90211090 instead would reverse this judgment."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "EU entries use CN8; Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code. Matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected"
"Helios Commodity Code (90211090) is explicitly documented as a migration-mapped default used \"where a local approved code was not supplied\""
"The automated check compared two incompatible nomenclature systems, producing a false-positive mismatch."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Ask the Swiss country trade owner to confirm 90211000 against a current Tares ruling (not just the working matrix)"
"scope the automated Helios-comparison rule to exclude Switzerland (or compare against the Swiss Matrix instead)"
"A ruling mandating 90211090 instead would reverse this judgment."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declared code (90211000) exactly matches Switzerland's own current approved classification" is well supported by the cited matrix, but the word "approved" remains subject to the submission's own caveat that the row may be only an internal working classification pending Tares confirmation.

"90211090 is an EU/migration-mapped master-data default, not a Swiss code" is somewhat broader than the evidence establishes: the evidence shows it is an EU-side/default value and that Swiss matching is not expected, but does not prove it can never be a valid Swiss code.
"to stop recurring false-positive flags on P1001/P1002/P1006" is not supported with product-specific evidence for P1002 or P1006.
"declared duty is already 0.0%, likely immaterial" is a reasonable qualification but duty treatment and any other tariff consequences were not independently verified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix may be an internal working classification rather than legally controlling, and a current Tares ruling or other authoritative Swiss source could require 90211090 or a different code; the available evidence therefore supports a likely jurisdiction/code-system mismatch but not definitive legal classification approval.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide exact row identifiers or quoted passages from each cited file and obtain the current Tares/ruling confirmation before changing the automated rule, while validating P1002 and P1006 separately rather than extrapolating from P1001.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the declaration details to "declaration.pdf" and the automated finding to "review_note.txt".
It identifies the specific register row "SD-SUP-02-P1006-2024" in "supplier_origin_register.csv" and states its origin, status, and validity date.
It explicitly records the limitation that the register caveat "doesn't prove no document exists outside the register."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission rejects the hypothesis that "The US-declared origin proves this preference claim is simply wrong" because manufacturing country and preferential origin can differ.
It separately rejects "No register hit means no supporting document exists" and "ERP manufacturing-country data can stand in for the missing supplier declaration."
It identifies unverified supplier route and preference scheme as evidence that "could reverse the judgment."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion is qualified as "not currently supported by available evidence," rather than declaring fraud or definitively invalidating the claim.
It states that the SUP-02 lookup "appears assumed, not verified in the packet" and that absence from the register does not prove absence elsewhere.
It acknowledges that a "valid, matching, unexpired document" could reverse the judgment.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission distinguishes "commercial declared origin, ERP manufacturing country, preferential rules-of-origin status."
It explains that brokers may claim preference "through the supplier route" separately from manufacturing country.

It identifies a data-lineage failure: the register is "not always updated when sourcing routes change," while relevant documents may reside in procurement's category folders rather than ClearView or the register.
The submission gives limited treatment to incentives or the precise mechanics of the applicable preference scheme.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: It recommends requesting the current supplier declaration "before relying on the Preference=Yes flag."
It correctly characterizes the immediate impact as "0.0% either way," making this a "documentation/compliance-risk fix, not a duty recovery."

The conditional recommendation to "correct or withdraw the preference claim" if no document is produced is prudent, but would be safer if it also required confirming the applicable scheme, rule, supplier route, and any alternative proof before withdrawal.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The only related supplier-declaration record found" is appropriately bounded to the materials searched, but the submission does not provide the search scope or exact register-search parameters beyond SUP-02/P1006 and the date.

The proposed withdrawal or correction step could be premature if procurement produces alternative proof, another supplier route is confirmed, or the applicable preference scheme permits evidence other than the requested declaration.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim may be valid: the US entry may describe manufacturing or commercial origin, while preferential origin could arise through a separate supplier route or applicable rule. The apparent absence of a current register or ClearView reference may reflect stale or incomplete system records rather than absence of supporting evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and verify the shipment's actual supplier/sourcing route and applicable preference scheme, then search the identified procurement repositories for matching evidence before recommending correction or withdrawal.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Even completed batches alone (n=220) run median 39.4h / mean 45.5h..." — cites batch_release.csv with specific counts and metrics, providing a traceable basis.

"QCore ... snapshot matches this export's timestamp exactly" — cites source_freshness.csv, but this claim conflicts with the non-coherent extract timing and is not reconciled with the rest of the evidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The apparent cycle time is survivorship-biased" and "the slowest, still-unresolved cases are excluded by construction" — correctly separates the observed completed-case metric from queue performance.
"open Riverbend batches are just recent arrivals... rejected" using the 78.6% past-36h statistic — tests a plausible alternative with evidence.
The analysis does not test the possibility that qcore_release_ts is an interface commit rather than the operational decision time, nor does it examine the pronounced release-hour concentration.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The table uses confidence labels such as "High" and "Medium-High" and says to "verify before using" the KPI, showing some caution.
"the backlog isn't a stale-extract artifact" and "snapshot matches this export's timestamp exactly" are too definitive given the extracts are not a coherent point-in-time snapshot.
The judgment also says all open batches "have already waited longer" than the claimed cycle time, while the evidence table says only 78.6% exceed 36 hours.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "verify before using 'about a day and a half' as a performance KPI" — appropriately reframes the decision away from immediate KPI adoption.
"ask Riverbend Quality what changed around July 20" and confirm whether cycle time starts at receipt or "evidence available" — proposes focused, potentially reversible checks.
The recommendation could better protect against optimizing a measurement artifact by requiring event/decision timestamps and aligned source snapshots before operational intervention.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: Rejected hypotheses include "The reported figure is a fair average of the current queue" and "The open Riverbend batches are just recent arrivals"; both are supported with relevant observations.

The strongest competing explanation—that release timestamps represent interface commits or are affected by batch timing—is not actively tested, and the source-freshness alternative is incorrectly treated as rejected.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Smallest useful check: ask Riverbend Quality what changed around July 20" is a focused query rather than a generic request for more data.
The request to confirm whether cycle time starts at receipt or evidence availability is relevant to KPI validity.

It omits the highest-value technical request: event-level evidence-available, decision, interface-commit, and release timestamps joined across a common snapshot, plus a profile of qcore_release_ts by hour.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "all ... open batches ... have already waited longer than the claimed cycle time itself" is overstated; the submission's own evidence says 78.6% exceed 36 hours, not all 42.

"QCore ... snapshot matches this export's timestamp exactly" and "the backlog isn't a stale-extract artifact" are unsupported or contradicted by the extract timing evidence indicating QCore and LabTrack are not the same snapshot.
"this single fact confirms whether it's a live operational problem versus a coincidence" overstates what a Riverbend interview alone can establish without event timestamps and synchronized extracts.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The backlog and completed-case statistics may reflect a real operational problem, but the apparent cycle time can also be distorted by qcore_release_ts being an interface commit rather than the evidence-available or decision timestamp. Non-coherent QCore/LabTrack snapshots could further distort joins and comparisons, so the current evidence does not cleanly distinguish workflow delay from measurement and extraction timing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain a synchronized event-level extract containing evidence-available, decision, interface-commit, and qcore release timestamps, then profile qcore_release_ts by hour (including the apparent 02:10 concentration). Use that test before attributing the KPI gap to Riverbend staffing, systems, or blocking exceptions.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live count refresh at Riverbend/Meridian ... could reveal newly-freed or newly-reserved MTR-4401 units"
"a direct check of HA-0022's true committed balance would resolve the BLT-7302 anomaly"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "only ~18% ($27,182) is cleanly actionable now from same-site stock" is not fully demonstrated in the submission because it does not show the row-level checks for UOM, qualification, revision, reservation, and storage constraints for every same-site candidate.

"The remaining ~60% ... is not transferable on current evidence" is appropriately qualified for current evidence, but some entries—especially BLT-7302 and potentially the servo-drive records—should be described as unavailable or blocked pending refresh rather than permanently non-transferable.

"A near-identical prior case ... confirms this exact failure mode recurs" supports the reservation-risk hypothesis but does not by itself establish that the current cases have the same operational outcome.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent opportunity may be larger than the current classification suggests if the five-week-old global stock snapshot is materially stale or if reserved inventory can be released after criticality review; conversely, some same-site candidates may also fail confirmation once live reservation, qualification, UOM, or revision checks are applied.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prioritized live validation of the highest-value candidates—starting with MTR-4401, BLT-7302, and the VLV-3722 rev A/rev B substitutions—using manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, current reservation/criticality, and committed balance, then report candidate value separately from confirmed actionable value with explicit pass/fail criteria.
